messages:
Maya (PM): quick sync: we need to lock MVP scope + launch gates for Optimize Toolkit focused on batching, caching, quantization recs, and eval-triggered alerts. customer asks piled up from ACME + Streamly. propose: narrow to 3 features for pilot and define acceptance criteria + owners. thoughts?
Josh (Eng-ML): +1. engineering constraints: batching heuristics + autoscaling hooks are highest effort. caching guidance (prefix/KV suggestions) is medium effort. quant profiles + regression checks = low-med but needs eval infra.
Carlos (Solutions): customers want prescriptive config snippets (examples for web chat, embeddings, reranking) and deterministic fallback guidance when quant causes quality hit. ACME specifically asked for an "easy switch" to fallback non-quant model on quality alerts.
Priya (SRE): operational must-haves: per-model token SLOs, alerting on sudden p50->p99 latency divergence, and telemetry for cache hit rates. we should require observability hooks for every recommendation.
Emma (Product Ops): draft acceptance criteria suggestion: 1) batching: 2 heuristic configs (latency-first, cost-first) with measured perf delta on pilot workload; 2) caching: documented prefix-KV playbook + invalidation examples; 3) quantization: 2 recommended profiles (fp16/4-bit) with automated eval-run and rollback on quality delta > 1.5% on baseline prompts; 4) eval-alerts: rules engine that triggers alert + automatic fallback to non-quant variant. docs + runbook required for all.
Taylor (Eng-Platform): feasibility notes: we can ship batching heuristics as config templates that plug into the router in ~3 sprints. caching playbook is mostly docs + a small sdk helper for prefix hashing (~1 sprint). quant profiles require per-model calibration jobs — need infra support but prototypeable.
Josh (Eng-ML): for the quality rollback threshold, suggest we define delta metric as decrease in exact-match or BLEU-like score on curated prompt set per customer. for chat, use normalized acceptability score from eval harness.
Maya (PM): good. let's pick pilot customers: ACME (high-safety) -> want conservative defaults (latency-first off, fallback automatic), Streamly (cost-sensitive) -> cost-first heuristics + quant suggested.
Carlos (Solutions): I'll coordinate the customer acceptance tests and produce sample workload traces. can validate acceptance criteria with them.
Priya (SRE): timeline: require instrumentation (cache hits, batch sizes, quant fallback events) to be in prod telemetry for pilot. spike to add metrics + dashboards by EOD next week.
Emma (Product Ops): proposed launch gates (must pass all): - pilot customers signed off on acceptance tests; - SLOs and dashboards in org console; - docs + runbooks published; - rollout plan with automatic fallback paths + owner.
Maya (PM): owners + immediate next actions: Josh -> batching heuristics prototype (due in 3w); Taylor -> caching SDK + dashboards (2w); Josh + Eng-ML -> quant profile prototype + eval hooks (3w); Carlos -> customer acceptance plan + traces (1w); Priya -> telemetry + alerting config (1.5w); Emma -> docs + runbook templates (1.5w).
Taylor (Eng-Platform): noted. will add PRD section for router config schema and sample yaml snippets.
Josh (Eng-ML): small code snippet we can include in docs for heuristic config:
```
batch_policy:
  name: latency-first
  max_batch_ms: 12
  max_tokens: 4096
  batching_window: adaptive
```
Priya (SRE): also adding these alerts to runbook:
- cache_hit_rate < 40% for 5m -> investigate
- quant_quality_delta > 1.5% -> trigger rollback and page oncall
Maya (PM): decision: MVP = batching templates + caching playbook + quant profile + eval-triggered alerting (with automatic fallback). scope reduced: no autoscaling policy UI in v1. agree?
Carlos (Solutions): agree from customer side. ACME still wants an explicit opt-out toggle for auto-fallback (they want manual review). we'll surface that in the runbook as an optional knob.
Emma (Product Ops): I'll schedule a pilot kickoff meeting with ACME + Streamly next Tue.
deploy-bot: Reminder: weekly roadmap sync in #product at 10am Wed :calendar_spiral:
Maya (PM): ok next steps captured. tagging owners in the PRD draft. will follow up with kickoff invite. :thumbsup:
